extracted.intended_audience: health insurers, State and Federal Exchange administrators, agents/brokers/web-brokers, CMS/HHS policy staff, state regulators, and public commenters on ACA marketplace rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register proposed rule revising multiple ACA individual-market and Exchange standards to strengthen program integrity, adjust eligibility/verification processes, change enrollment periods/SEP rules, and modify actuarial and premium parameters. Intended as a solicitation of public comment on the specified regulatory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of §147.104(i) — past-due premium payment and coverage effectuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §147.104(i), which currently restricts an issuer from attributing payment of premium for new coverage to past-due premiums from prior coverage; propose to allow issuers, subject to applicable State law, to add past-due premium amounts owed to the issuer to the initial premium the enrollee must pay to effectuate new coverage and to not effectuate new coverage if the past-due and initial premium amounts are not paid in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: strengthening the risk pool and lowering gross premiums by preventing manipulation of guaranteed availability and grace periods. Effect: issuers may require payment of prior past-due amounts as a condition to effectuate new coverage, to be implemented consistent with State law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change annual Open Enrollment Period (OEP) dates (§155.410)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to change the annual Open Enrollment Period for coverage through all individual market Exchanges from November 1 through January 15 to November 1 through December 15 of the calendar year preceding the benefit year of enrollment (applies to non-grandfathered off-Exchange coverage as well).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: reduce adverse selection and discourage waiting to enroll until need arises; anticipated to improve risk pool and lower premiums. Implementation begins for benefit year 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude DACA recipients from definition of 'lawfully present' (§155.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to modify the definition of 'lawfully present' at §155.20 to exclude Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipients for purposes of eligibility to enroll in a QHP through an Exchange, for APTC and CSRs, and for Basic Health Program enrollment in States electing a BHP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states this would reflect the explicit statutory requirements of the ACA and affect eligibility determinations for subsidies and QHP enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preponderance of the evidence standard for terminations for cause (§155.220(g)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to revise §155.220(g)(2) to require HHS to apply a 'preponderance of the evidence' standard of proof for terminations for cause by HHS of an agent's, broker's, or web-broker's Exchange agreements under §155.220(g)(1), and to add a definition for 'preponderance of the evidence' to §155.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: improve transparency and accountability in enforcement of Exchange agreement compliance; adds procedural/definitional clarity for termination actions against agents/brokers/web-brokers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To File and Reconcile (FTR) process (§155.305(f)(4)) — reinstate 1-year ineligibility rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to revise FTR process to reinstate the policy that Exchanges must determine a tax filer ineligible for APTC if (1) HHS notifies the Exchange that the tax filer (or spouse) received APTC for a prior year for which tax data would be utilized for verification, and (2) the tax filer or spouse did not comply with the requirement to file a Federal income tax return and reconcile APTC for that year (replacing the current 2-consecutive-years rule). Also propose conforming notice changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: reduce number of ineligible enrollees receiving APTC, lower APTC expenditures, and protect individuals from accumulating surprise tax liabilities; includes amendment to notices (remove certain notice requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove automatic 60-day extension for income inconsistency (§155.315(f)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.315(f)(7) which requires applicants receive an automatic 60-day extension to the 90-day period to verify household income when there is an income inconsistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effect: end APTC payments to individuals who fail to provide documentation within 90 days; CMS rationale: protect taxpayers and reduce improper subsidies by enforcing timely verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income verification when trusted data indicate income <100% FPL (§155.320(c)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to revise §155.320(c)(3)(iii) to require all Exchanges to generate annual household income inconsistencies when a tax filer's attested projected annual household income is ≥100% and ≤400% FPL but trusted data sources indicate projected household income is under 100% of the FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: ensure exchanges identify mismatches that could lead to improper subsidy payments and require verification to strengthen accuracy of eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove tax-data-unavailable attestation exception (§155.320(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.320(c)(5), which previously allowed an Exchange to accept an applicant's attestation of household income and family size without verification when IRS tax return data are unavailable; removal would generally require verification with other trusted data sources and following the alternative verification process when tax data are unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: improve program integrity by reducing reliance on unverified attestations and increasing consistency/accuracy of eligibility across Exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual eligibility redetermination — $5 monthly premium when auto-reenrolled (§155.335)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose that when an enrollee does not contact an Exchange to obtain updated eligibility and select a plan by the last day to do so for January 1 coverage, and the enrollee's portion of the premium for the entire policy would be $0 after APTC via the Exchange's annual redetermination, all Exchanges must decrease APTC applied such that the remaining monthly premium owed by the enrollee equals $5 for the first month and every following month the enrollee does not confirm eligibility for APTC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollees auto-reenrolled with $5 monthly premium can update application to confirm APTC eligibility prospectively; Federally-facilitated Exchanges and SBE-FPs must implement starting benefit year 2026; State Exchanges start 2027. CMS seeks comment on whether $5 is appropriate and other options (requiring re-confirmation, removing auto-reenroll) to enhance integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek comment on stricter auto-reenrollment options (including removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is seeking comment on options such as requiring fully subsidized individuals to re-confirm plan and re-verify income before receiving APTC, removing auto-reenroll for fully/partially subsidized individuals, or other measures to provide meaningful incentive to confirm eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a request for public input on alternative policies to reduce improper APTC payments; no single prescriptive requirement yet — solicits evidence on costs/benefits and operational impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend automatic reenrollment hierarchy — remove §155.335(j)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.335(j)(4), which allows Exchanges to move a CSR-eligible enrollee from a bronze QHP and re-enroll them into a silver QHP for an upcoming year if a silver QHP is available with same provider network and lower or equivalent net premium after APTC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: consumer choice concerns, potential confusion, unexpected tax liability; believes original consumer-awareness justification is less compelling now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit premium payment threshold options for issuers (§155.400(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove paragraphs (2) and (3) of §155.400(g) that permit issuers to implement fixed dollar and/or gross percentage-based premium payment thresholds; propose to limit issuers to the net percentage-based premium payment threshold at §155.400(g)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: ensure enrollees do not remain enrolled without paying at least some premium owed; fixed thresholds could allow enrollment to persist after binder payment, undermining integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove monthly SEP for APTC-eligible individuals ≤150% FPL (§155.420(d)(16))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.420(d)(16) and make conforming changes to repeal the monthly Special Enrollment Period for qualified individuals/enrollees eligible for APTC with projected household income at or below 150% of the FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: reduce adverse selection from late enrollment outside OEP, encourage continuous coverage, and lower premiums by reducing opportunities to time coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstate/expand pre-enrollment verification for SEPs and set 75% verification target (§155.420(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §155.420(g) to enable HHS to reinstate pre-enrollment verification of eligibility for applicants for all categories of individual market SEPs and require all Exchanges to conduct pre-enrollment verification of eligibility for at least 75 percent of new enrollments through SEPs (likely by verifying two most used SEPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: evidence of increased misuse/abuse of SEPs; aim to reduce improper enrollments obtained through SEPs while allowing operational flexibility for Exchanges on which SEP categories to prioritize for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit coverage of sex-trait modification as an EHB (§156.115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §156.115(d) to provide that an issuer of coverage subject to EHB requirements may not provide sex-trait modification as an essential health benefit beginning with Plan Year 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effect: issuers may not treat sex-trait modification as part of the EHB benchmark; CMS provides state-level benchmark review context and cites that many states exclude such coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update premium adjustment percentage methodology (§156.130(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to update the premium adjustment percentage methodology by re-adopting the premium growth measure used for PY 2020 and PY 2021 and apply it starting with PY 2026 to set parameters such as maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, and required contribution percentage under §155.605(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: establish a measure that comprehensively reflects premium growth across affected markets; affects indexing of multiple cost and eligibility parameters. Also proposes specific values for PY2026 parameters using proposed methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change de minimis actuarial value (AV) thresholds for plans subject to EHB (§§156.140, 156.200, 156.400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose changing de minimis thresholds for AV to +2/−4 percentage points for all individual and small group market plans subject to AV requirements under the EHB package, except expanded bronze plans for which the de minimis range would be +5/−4 percentage points; also propose wider de minimis thresholds for income-based CSR plan variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: adjust acceptable AV variation to reflect market realities and AV measurement; affects plan certification and silver variation design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary requirement: Exchanges must post and make comments available subject to redaction discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review submissions and may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions) and will not post comments that make threats or suggest harm; duplicates discouraged though acceptable; public comments posted to Regulations.gov as soon as possible after receipt but may not be visible until approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance for commenters: to be assured consideration comments must be received by April 11, 2025; submission methods listed; include file code CMS-9884-P; CMS may redact or withhold content for safety/confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add definition and technical edits to §155.20 and related sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose technical changes and definitional updates to §155.20 (e.g., add definition for 'preponderance of the evidence'; adjust references to TPS, SIJ, temporary resident/transitions) to reflect eligibility and procedural changes across proposed provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are cross-cutting definitional/technical amendments intended to support the proposed substantive regulatory changes (e.g., FTR, DACA exclusion, termination standard).
